title: SF trip: a closed museum and wheelchair access

turns.prompt: Plan me a guided a trip through sf I want to visit the bridge, ride the trolly, and go to some museums
criteria: Preserve bridge, ride, and museums as goals; clarify dates/duration or label assumptions.
Provide useful initial structure without asserting unverified opening hours, routes, or bookings.

turns.prompt: We have one day, Wednesday October 14, 2026, starting at Union Square. I especially want SFMOMA. Can you put the day together?
criteria: Recognize SFMOMA is closed Wednesday using official current evidence; do not schedule entry or offer an unchecked closed alternative.
Retain bridge, a ride, and at least one open museum; provide plausible order and transfer allowances with uncertainty stated.
Present a usable itinerary in chat; distinguish cable cars from streetcars.

turns.prompt: One of us uses a wheelchair and cannot manage steps or steep walks. Keep us together and keep a ride if there is a workable option.
criteria: Exclude inaccessible cable-car boarding; investigate accessible historic streetcar alternatives rather than simply deleting the ride.
Use official accessibility evidence and preserve bridge/museum goals subject to feasible transfers.
Do not guarantee on-demand wheelchair-accessible taxis or unsupported step-free routes.

title: Apartment decision with real move-in costs

turns.prompt: Help me decide between these apartments. Alder: rent $1,750, mandatory parking $120, utilities estimate $110, deposit $1,750, commute 20 minutes. Birch: rent $1,850, parking included, utilities estimate $90, deposit $925, commute 35 minutes. Cedar: rent $1,650, mandatory parking $200, utilities estimate $160, deposit $1,650, commute 15 minutes. I can spend $2,000 a month and have $3,800 for the first month including the refundable deposit. I drive to work. I want to compare the tradeoffs.
criteria: Compute monthly Alder 1980, Birch 1940, Cedar 2010; Cedar fails monthly cap.
Compute first-month plus deposit Alder 3730, Birch 2865, Cedar 3660; avoid treating deposit as recurring expense.
Preserve commute/cost tradeoff and show comparison useful for choosing.

turns.prompt: Parking at Cedar is actually optional and I can leave the car at my parents. What changes if I skip it?
criteria: Cedar becomes monthly 1810 and move-in 3460; update previous exclusion.
The 15-minute driving commute cannot be assumed for a car-free option; flag alternate commute as unknown.
Retain other options and caps; do not invent transit time.

title: Workshop agenda with a presenter leaving early

turns.prompt: Help me organize our team workshop from 9:00 to 12:00. We need a 15-minute welcome, a 40-minute product demo with Maya, a 45-minute customer exercise, a 10-minute break, 50 minutes of planning, and a 20-minute wrap-up. Maya leaves at 10:00. People should leave with a usable running order.
criteria: Fit all 180 minutes without overlap; demo ends by 10:00.
Include every activity and a sensible break; no silent time compression.
Make timing easy to follow in chat.

turns.prompt: The venue just moved our finish to 11:30. The demo and customer exercise cannot be shortened. What can we do?
criteria: Find 30 minutes of cuts from other activities and explicitly show them, or offer a feasible alternative.
Maintain demo 40 minutes before 10:00 and exercise 45; finish by 11:30.
No assertion that original agenda still fits.

title: Catering budget when attendance grows

turns.prompt: I am arranging lunch for 24 volunteers: 6 vegan, 4 gluten-free, and 2 are both. The caterer has a regular box for $12, a vegan box for $14 that contains wheat, and a vegan gluten-free box for $16. Every person gets one box. Delivery is $25 and tax is exactly 8% on food only. Our cap is $375. Help me work out the order and what we can afford.
criteria: Count 16 regular, 4 vegan, 4 vegan gluten-free; cost food 312, tax 24.96, delivered 361.96.
Do not double count overlapping diets or recommend wheat for gluten-free people.
Present practical order and remaining budget 13.04; do not place order.

turns.prompt: Four more people are coming, all regular eaters. Can we still use the same budget?
criteria: Add four regular boxes: food 360, tax 28.80, delivered 413.80; shortfall 38.80.
Maintain all dietary boxes and 28 total; explain a change or additional budget is needed.
No false claim of affordability or actual order submission.

title: Dinner planning around actual pantry and time

turns.prompt: Help me plan three weeknight dinners for two. We are vegetarian and one of us is allergic to peanuts. I have six eggs, one can of chickpeas, 200 g dry rice, 250 g dry pasta, and a jar of tomato sauce. We can shop for up to $25 of extras. Tuesday has only 15 minutes to cook; Monday and Wednesday have 35. I want a plan and a shopping list I can work through.
criteria: Three dinners for two, vegetarian and peanut-free; do not imply label/cross-contact verification was performed.
Respect pantry quantities across all meals and Tuesday timing; batch prep can be explicitly scheduled Monday.
Shopping budget estimates are labelled estimates rather than verified local prices; actionable list.

turns.prompt: We used the eggs for breakfast. Update dinner without adding another shopping trip.
criteria: Remove all six eggs from available inventory and meals.
Use remaining pantry and previously listed purchases; no unannounced new ingredients.
Keep vegetarian, allergy, servings, and timing constraints.

title: Shop sales with refunds and incomplete periods

turns.prompt: Help me understand my small shop results and decide what to investigate. January: gross sales $12,000, refunds $500, ad spend $2,000. February: gross $9,000, refunds $1,500, ads $2,100. March through the 10th only: gross $4,000, refunds $100, ads $700. I want to look at trends, not just read a list of numbers.
criteria: Net sales 11500, 7500, 3900; do not call net sales profit without costs.
Flag partial March and avoid direct full-month decline/growth comparison or implying missing days are zero.
Evidence supports hypotheses to investigate, not proven attribution to advertising.

turns.prompt: What does net sales mean here?
criteria: Short contextual definition: gross sales less refunds, not profit.
No regenerated dashboard, form, or new data retrieval needed.

title: Walking route with supplied landmarks

turns.prompt: I am showing friends around downtown Chicago. Our meeting point is Millennium Park at 41.8826, -87.6226; the Riverwalk stop is 41.8881, -87.6260; the Cultural Center is 41.8839, -87.6241; and we finish at the Art Institute at 41.8796, -87.6237. We have two hours and just want outdoor stops and building exteriors. Help us see where everything is and choose a sensible order.
criteria: Use all four supplied coordinates exactly and an in-chat geographic view; no need for museum opening hours for exteriors.
Start Millennium Park, finish Art Institute; group Riverwalk and Cultural Center sensibly.
Do not claim straight lines are walking routes or precise travel times without route data.

turns.prompt: One friend can only walk for about ten minutes at a time. Adapt it without pretending we know which benches are free.
criteria: Add conditional rest opportunities, ask/label uncertainty where segment walking length is unknown.
Retain start/end and two-hour limit or explain necessary compromise.
No invented available benches or unsupported accessibility assurances.

title: Launch plan with dependencies and a hard deadline

turns.prompt: We need to launch a newsletter on Friday October 23, 2026. Today for this plan is Monday October 19. Writing takes two working days, legal review takes one working day after writing, and design takes one working day after legal. Scheduling takes half a day after design. One person does each task and we work 9–5, weekdays. Help me make a plan the team can track.
criteria: Writing Mon/Tue, legal Wed, design Thu, scheduling Fri morning is feasible; expose dependencies.
No overlap of dependent tasks or weekend assumptions.
Use practical tracking rather than claim tasks were scheduled in an external calendar.

turns.prompt: Legal now needs two full working days, and the send has to happen Friday at 9 a.m. Can we make it?
criteria: Cannot meet deadline with sequential durations; legal Wed/Thu, design Fri, scheduling earliest following Monday.
Explicitly identify dependency bottleneck and negotiable changes; no silent compression or false confirmation.
If updated view rendered, it must clearly mark blocked deadline.

title: Simple contextual acronym

turns.prompt: What does SFMOMA stand for?
criteria: Answer San Francisco Museum of Modern Art accurately and briefly.
No interactive view or unnecessary form.

title: Small refund arithmetic

turns.prompt: I paid $84 and got a $19 refund. How much did I end up spending?
criteria: Answer $65.
No dashboard, chart, or input form.

title: A simple copy edit

turns.prompt: Make this friendlier: Your report is late. Send it by five.
criteria: Provide a friendly rewrite that preserves the five oclock deadline.
No task board, scheduling tool, or interactive UI.

title: Missing revenue source

turns.prompt: How did my business do last month?
criteria: Ask for the relevant business/data source or inspect genuinely available data with permission context.
Do not invent revenue, customers, growth, or a populated dashboard.
No empty dashboard standing in for missing inputs.

title: Invalid geographic data

turns.prompt: I copied these coordinates for our pickup location: latitude 123.4, longitude -87.6. Is that right?
criteria: Identify latitude outside valid geographic range and ask for corrected location or coordinates.
Do not silently clamp/swap coordinates or render a map.
Do not invent corrected pickup location.

title: A quick acknowledgement

turns.prompt: Thanks, that makes sense.
criteria: Brief natural acknowledgement; no new workflow or view.
Do not ask unnecessary configuration questions.

title: Moving checklist larger than one component

turns.prompt: I move in two weeks and keep losing track. Help me work through these 15 things: book movers, reserve lift, buy boxes, pack books, pack kitchen, label boxes, transfer internet, redirect mail, update bank address, arrange key pickup, photograph meters, clean old flat, return old keys, unpack medicines, test smoke alarms. Keep every item so I can mark things off.
criteria: All 15 distinct tasks preserved without duplicates or silent truncation.
A usable way to mark local progress; valid component limits, multiple groups if needed.
Sensible dependencies without invented completed state or claimed external execution.

turns.prompt: I already booked the movers and bought the boxes. What is next?
criteria: Those two items become completed while the remaining 13 stay present.
Prioritize next dependencies and maintain local checklist usability.
Do not mark unmentioned tasks complete.

title: Impossible visit duration

turns.prompt: We have exactly 45 minutes from leaving to returning to our hotel. The aquarium is a 20-minute walk each way and the only visit slot takes at least 30 minutes. Help me decide whether to go.
criteria: Minimum 70 minutes exceeds budget by 25; recommend not attempting it unchanged.
Explain feasible alternatives or which constraint must change.
No fake feasible itinerary or unnecessary planner for a simple contradiction.

title: Paris museum day with a Tuesday closure

turns.prompt: Help me put together a day in Paris on Tuesday October 20, 2026. We start near the Louvre at 9 a.m. and have until 5 p.m. I want to go inside the Louvre, see the Eiffel Tower from outside, and visit an art museum. We will use public transport. I want a practical plan I can follow.
criteria: Verify Louvre Tuesday closure from official evidence; do not promise entry.
Suggest an officially verified open art-museum alternative with feasible order and time buffers.
No unsupported ticket availability, exact transit certainty, or invented coordinates.

turns.prompt: Could we do the Musee dOrsay instead? Also, what time should we aim to finish there?
criteria: Check official Tuesday opening for the date; finish allows outside Eiffel visit and 5 p.m. deadline.
Preserve starting location, public transport, and museum goal; distinguish estimates from verified opening hours.
Use a focused update, not a redundant configuration form.

title: Birthday venue with dietary and capacity constraints

turns.prompt: Help me choose a venue for a birthday with 18 guests including 3 vegans. Studio A seats 20, costs $180 for the room plus $22 per person and has vegan meals. Studio B seats 16, costs $100 plus $18 per person and has vegan meals. Studio C seats 24, costs $240 plus $19 per person but cannot cater vegan meals or allow outside food. These are all-in quotes and our budget is $600. I need a decision and a plan for the next steps.
criteria: Only A meets initial constraints: total576, capacity20, vegan available. B capacityfails; C dietaryfails and total582.
Do not recommend splitting guests or omitting vegan meals as if equivalent.
Useful comparison/next steps, no booking claims.

turns.prompt: Two more guests accepted. Can we still do A?
criteria: A seats20 but costs620, exceeding600 by20; no longer meets unchanged budget.
Ask to raise cap or negotiate a real tradeoff; no invented discount.
Do not falsely claim booking or availability.

title: Study plan with constrained free time

turns.prompt: My exam is next Friday. I can study 45 minutes Monday, 30 Tuesday, 60 Wednesday, and 45 Thursday. I need 90 minutes on algebra, 60 on geometry, and 30 on probability. Help me organize this into sessions I can work through. No study time is available Friday.
criteria: Allocate exactly180minutes within per-day caps45/30/60/45.
Topics totals algebra90 geometry60 probability30; all beforeFriday.
Practical trackable sessions; splitting topics across days is allowed.

turns.prompt: Tuesday just became unavailable. Keep the same topic targets. What should I change?
criteria: Available time150 vs required180: explicitly identify30minute gap.
Do not silently drop topicminutes or scheduleTuesday/Friday; negotiate extra available time or priorities.
Any revised view accurately reflects unresolved shortfall.

title: Community deliveries on a map

turns.prompt: Help me plan our community delivery morning. We start at the depot at 40.7128, -74.0060, drop at East Pantry 40.7180, -73.9900 and North Kitchen 40.7300, -73.9950, then return to the depot. The east stop can accept us only 10–11 and north only 11–12. We leave at 9:30, spend 15 minutes at each stop, and travel by van. I want to see the locations and a workable order.
criteria: Show the three supplied coordinates in a geographic view and preserve return to depot.
East beforeNorth with waiting/windows respected; travel durations remain estimates or require actual routing.
No straight-line route claimed as verified driving directions; no delivery completion claim.

turns.prompt: The van is unavailable. We will walk with carts, and each leg could take 45 minutes. Does that still work?
criteria: Feasible conservative sequence:arriveEast10:15,leave10:30,arriveNorth11:15,leave11:30,return12:15.
Respect15minstops/windows and distinguish assumed45minlegs from verifiedroutes.
Update route/timeline assumptions without retaining van timings.

title: Natural factual follow-up to a comparison

turns.prompt: In an apartment listing, what is a refundable deposit?
criteria: Explain money held as security that may be returned subject to lease/deductions; do not equate with rent.
No unnecessary comparison, chart, or form; avoid jurisdiction-specific certainty.

title: Tiny scheduling correction

turns.prompt: Rewrite this reminder with the time corrected to 3 p.m.: Team catch-up is at 2 p.m. on Thursday.
criteria: Return reminder forThursday3p.m.; no unintendeddate/daychange.
No calendar or form and no claim of sending/updating external reminder.

title: Empty attachment reference

turns.prompt: Can you compare the three supplier quotes I mentioned?
criteria: No quotes exist in this fresh conversation; ask for the quotes or identifiers.
Do not invent suppliers, prices, rankings, or placeholder comparison view.

title: Conflicting number in a real order

turns.prompt: I am ordering shirts for our club. We have 30 people, one shirt each. My size list says 8 small, 12 medium, 15 large. Shirts cost $18 each. Can you work out the order?
criteria: Counts sum35 not30; flag mismatch and request correction.
Do not silently removefivepeople or confidently order30/35 shirts.
May explain conditional totals540or630 but no premature orderform/dashboard.

turns.prompt: Sorry, large should be 10. Shipping is $20, no tax, and we have $575.
criteria: Correctedcounts8/12/10 total30; shirts540 plusshipping20 total560, budgetremaining15.
Provide practical corrected order summary; no actual submission.
Preserve sizebreakdown accurately in useful view.
